newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait names new cabinet, changes oil and defence.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait names new cabinet, changes oil and defence.

text.p: Kuwait on Tuesday named a 14-man cabinet, giving the oil, defence and interior portfolios to new ministers while the foreign minister kept his post, an official decree said.
The cabinet, formed after last week's parliamentary election, is headed by Crown Prince Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al- Sabah and includes another four members of the ruling al-Sabah family.

By law the new cabinet must include at least one of the 50 elected MPs. Four of the ministers are elected deputies while the others become ex-officio members of the all-male parliament which will hold its first session on October 20.

U.S.-educated Issa Mazeedi, a member of Kuwait's minority Shi'ite branch of Islam, will head the key Oil Ministry. OPEC- member Kuwait currently produces about two million barrels a day, the state's main revenue earner.
Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah, a brother to Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah, was named first deputy prime minister and Foreign Minister, an official decree said.

Nasser Abdulla al-Rodhan kept his post as Finance Minister and is one of three deputy prime ministers. The other deputy is Sheikh Salem Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah, a former foreign minister, who was named Defence Minister.

Sheikh Mohammad Khaled al-Hamad al-Sabah, also a member of the ruling family, was made Interior Minister while Sheikh Saud Nasser al-Saud al-Sabah, who served as ambassador to Washington during the Gulf crisis, kept the Information Ministry. He is also acting health minister.
